narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Mark; brisk, plain storytelling, including his own Scripture citations.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Jesus of Nazareth, about thirty; calm authority, teaching, commanding and healing.

unclean-spirit.name: Unclean spirit
unclean-spirit.note: Demon(s) crying out through the possessed on recognising Jesus; shrieking, terrified.

friends-of-jesus.name: Jesus' friends
friends-of-jesus.note: His own people who set out to lay hold on him; alarmed, dismissive.

scribes.name: Scribes
scribes.note: Teachers of the law; suspicious and accusing.

crowd.name: Crowd
crowd.note: The people gathered around Jesus in Capharnaum; amazed, or relaying a message to him.

1.t: And he entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had a withered hand.

2.t: And they watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath-day: that they might accuse him.

3.t: And he saith to the man who had the withered hand:

4.t: Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath-day, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy?

5.t: And looking round about on them with anger, being grieved for the blindness of their hearts, he saith to the man:
And he stretched it forth; and his hand was restored unto him.

6.t: And the Pharisees going out immediately, made a consultation with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

7.t: But Jesus retired with his disciples to the sea; and a great multitude followed him from Galilee and Judea,

8.t: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan: and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing the things which he did, came to him.

9.t: And he spoke to his disciples that a small ship should wait on him, because of the multitude, lest they should throng him:

10.t: For he healed many, so that they pressed upon him to touch him, as many as had evils.

11.t: And the unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him: and they cried, saying:

12.t: Thou art the Son of God.
12.q: Many unclean spirits cry out together here; the canonical singular id is used

12.t: And he strictly charged them that they should not make him known.

13.t: And going up into a mountain, he called unto him whom he would himself: and they came to him.

14.t: And he made that twelve should be with him: and that he might send them to preach.

15.t: And he gave them power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils.

16.t: And to Simon he gave the name of Peter:

17.t: And James, the son of Zebedee, and John, the brother of James; and he named them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

18.t: And Andrew and Philip, and Bartholomew and Matthew, and Thomas, and James, of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Cananean:

19.t: And Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

20.t: And they come to a house: and the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

21.t: And when his friends had heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said:

21.q: "They said" may mean his friends/kin or people in general; taken as his friends

22.t: And the Scribes, who were come down from Jerusalem, said:
He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of devils he casteth out devils.

23.t: And after he had called them together, he said to them in parables:
How can Satan cast out Satan?

24.t: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

25.t: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

26.t: And if Satan be risen up against himself, he is divided, and cannot stand, but hath an end.

27.t: No man can enter into the house of a strong man, and rob him of his goods, unless he first bind the strong man, and then shall he plunder his house.

28.t: Amen, I say to you, that all sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and the blasphemies wherewith they shall blaspheme:

29.t: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost, shall never have forgiveness, but shall be guilty of an everlasting sin.

30.q: Narrator's aside recalling the scribes' charge from 3:22

31.t: And his mother and his brethren came: and standing without, sent to him, calling him.

32.t: And the multitude sat about him: and they say to him:
Behold thy mother and thy brethren, without, seek for thee.

33.t: Who is my mother and my brethren?

34.t: And looking round on them who sat about him, he saith:
Behold my mother and my brethren.

35.t: For whosoever shall do the will of God, he is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
